# Corpus programs whose STDOUT is not a function of the compiler, so the
# arm64 flat-vs-ssa differential compares their exit status only. Read by
# internal/e2e/arm64_ssa_differential_test.go; format is `<path>  <reason>`.
#
# This is NOT an allowlist for a wrong answer. A program that prints something
# different under the two backends belongs in
# arm64-ssa-diff-known-divergences.txt; a program that prints something
# different on two runs of the SAME binary belongs here, because comparing it
# would report a flake as a compiler bug. Rows still run under both backends,
# still count toward the leg's floor, and a crash or a wrong exit code under
# either backend is still caught.
#
# Verified against the corpus: a row naming a program the walk does not find
# fails the test, so a rename cannot leave a row that can never fire.
#
# Determinism is checked by running the flat build twice, not asserted — the
# two timing rows below usually agree with themselves, which is exactly why
# they are dangerous: they would fail rarely and look like a real divergence.

examples/cli/yes.fern  writes its line forever, so stdout is however much the harness captured before the timeout kill
examples/wasm/echo_handler.fern  an HTTP server: it listens until it is killed
examples/wasm/native_http_handler.fern  an HTTP server: it listens until it is killed
examples/wasm/url_router.fern  an HTTP server: it listens until it is killed
examples/tests/batch8_test.fern  prints the path of a per-run temp directory; the unique suffix is a monotonic-clock reading on the flat backend and 8 random hex digits on arm64ssa, and neither repeats
examples/tests/bench_test.fern  prints measured elapsed times
examples/tests/rel_tol_and_ms_bench_test.fern  prints measured elapsed times
